verifiedBehavior: RELATION candidates are searched and paged by a dedicated server endpoint that resolves the source relation display field, relation filter, target module permission, tenant/system boundary and data scope; the client performs no fallback filtering.
A required aggregate stays local until scalar, relation and minimum subtable requirements are complete, then creates atomically instead of emitting an invalid early autosave.

RELATION detail exposes the configured display value and not the technical target id; REFERENCE exposes value plus READY state; SUBTABLE renders a desktop grid and mobile cards from server-paged rows.
Creating a module copy now allocates neutral field ids before applying exact structured contracts, preserving same-module field references without weakening publication validation.
The accepted ordinary-member composition survives a packaged backend restart with the same canonical API values and responsive UI.

resolvedFindings.finding: The initial picker reused generic target-module q, which correctly rejects a readable display field that is not declared searchable.
resolvedFindings.resolution: A source-relation candidate endpoint now applies display/filter/scope semantics on the server; positive and restricted-member checks plus the browser journey passed.

resolvedFindings.finding: Scalar blur could start autosave before the required relation and minimum subtable row had been staged.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Initial autosave now waits for the complete required aggregate, while subsequent edits retain normal autosave behavior.

resolvedFindings.finding: The legacy two-phase copy created structured fields with required properties removed, conflicting with exact P4-C3 validation.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Copy first allocates neutral TEXT drafts, then applies fully remapped exact field definitions; targeted and full integration tests passed.
